facts.event: COVID immediate operating and workforce response
facts.value: Due to lower traffic and temporary store closures, the company reduced store and associate hours, furloughed approximately 40% of central-office, distribution-center and store employees, and withdrew FY2020 guidance.

Effective April 12, 2020, James Conroy (President and CEO) accepted a temporary 50% base-salary reduction; other named executive/senior executives were reduced 25%. Annual cash performance bonuses for FY2020 management were deferred no later than September 1, 2020; non-employee directors waived the current-quarter cash retainer. Board and Compensation Committee approved these actions April 7, 2020. The filing’s exhibits include temporary salary-consent forms for John Hazen and other executives.

facts.event: Pandemic risk and digital/operational continuity context
facts.value: FY2021 10-K states COVID-related restrictions materially affected western events and could require furloughs, reduced hours, closures, expense reductions and discounting. It describes the company’s e-commerce sites and its upgraded e-commerce platform as the foundation for digital storefronts. John Hazen’s April 2020 salary-consent form evidences that he was then a senior executive; later official disclosures identify him as CDO from 2018 until Interim CEO in November 2024.
